ch00.card: Start here. What you are about to see.
ch00.s01.c1: This is a research project. It is building a language model. That is a program that reads text and writes an answer.
ch00.s01.c2: Two of its goals are skills and careful thinking first, then learning from only a few examples.
ch00.s01.c3: It is not an app. GitHub lists 0 releases for it, and nothing here is finished.
ch00.s02.c1: First goal: skills and careful thinking.
ch00.s02.c2: At the smallest size, 3 million learned numbers, an earlier design scored higher than an ordinary same-size model. It did so in all six separate training runs.
ch00.s02.c3: Second goal: learning from only a few examples. This is only partly shown so far. Brand-new kinds of rule are mostly missed.
ch00.s06.c1: The reader gives each letter a meaning from the whole question. Its main part is borrowed from others and frozen. Our practice never changes it.
ch00.s06.c2: The thinker thinks in rounds, which are laps of looking and thinking. Our practice sets its settings from scratch.
ch00.s06.c3: The calculator is ordinary code, not AI. It takes a text request and replies with text.
ch00.s06.c4: The stop switch says done. It is built, but never run.
ch00.s06.c5: The talker writes the final answer. Today it is only a small stand-in, a placeholder for the real thing.
ch00.s08.c1: One picture runs through the whole video: a student doing a word problem.
ch00.s08.c2: A translator reads the question. Then a team of note-takers thinks it over, round after round.
ch00.s08.c3: The call writer, our team leader, writes a request slip. A pocket calculator hands back a slip with the result.
ch00.s08.c4: A little bell rings when they are done. One person writes the final answer. Each colour always means the same part. Remember, the cards are an analogy, not a diagram of the code.
ch00.s09.c1: Green means tested, and a result file exists. For example, with the calculator outside, scores matched the earlier design in 6 runs, at the smallest size.
ch00.s09.c2: Amber means built, but never tested. The code exists, but no real training run was ever done. An example is the stop switch.
ch00.s09.c3: Grey means placeholder. It does not exist yet. An example is the English talker, which is planned, not built.
ch00.s11.c1: A vector is a list of numbers, like a note card. The reader turns each letter into one. Picture only means a drawing, not a measurement.
ch00.s11.c2: A round is one lap of looking at the whole question, passing notes, and thinking. The thinker does several laps.
ch00.s12.c1: A call is a text request to the calculator. Here, sub 12 5 means: take 5 away from 12.
ch00.s12.c2: The reply is the calculator's answer, also text: 7. Together they read sub 12 5 = 7.
ch00.s12.c3: The model writes calls itself. It may also write nothing, when no exact arithmetic is needed.
ch00.s13.c1: Practice means the model tries a question, is told the right answer, and every setting is nudged a tiny bit. One nudge is one update.
ch00.s13.c2: Questions kept aside are never used in practice. They are saved for the exam, so the score is fair. The model has never seen them.
ch00.s14.c1: A score is points out of 100, the share of questions answered right. Here, 73.01 points on 6,040 questions kept aside.
ch00.s14.c2: A copy is one separate run of the model from its own random start. Six copies are six chances to see the same result.
ch00.s14.c3: Careful: 73.01 is one copy, at the smallest size, on an earlier design.
ch00.s15.c1: A plain model is an ordinary model of the same size, trained on the same practice, with the same borrowed reader. It is our yardstick.
ch00.s15.c2: On the same 6,040 questions kept aside, the plain model scored 67.12 points out of 100, and ours scored 73.01.
ch00.s15.c3: Careful: these two scores come from one copy, at the smallest size, on an earlier design. We do not claim it holds at bigger sizes.
ch00.s19.c1: Every real number in this video comes from a project file. Here is one example: the plain model's score, traced to its file.
ch00.s19.c2: Pictures that only illustrate carry a tag, like picture only or made-up example. They are never real measurements.
ch00.s19.c3: What is not proven stays amber or grey. Nothing here is released, and no future date is promised to you.
